description: A rich and creamy Indian curry, Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani) is a globally loved dish known for its succulent tandoor-cooked chicken bathed in a velvety tomato-based sauce. This classic recipe delivers authentic flavors, blending aromatic spices with butter and cream for an unforgettable culinary experience. It is perfect for a comforting family meal or entertaining guests.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste, 1 tbsp Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric powder, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat the chicken. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 tablespoon of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes until browned and cooked through. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil and 1 tablespoon of butter. Add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in 1 tbsp ginger garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Gravy
instructions.text: Add the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, cumin powder, coriander powder, sugar, and water or chicken broth to the pan. Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Stir occasionally.

instructions.title: Blend and Strain the Gravy
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender to blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing down to extract all liquid and discarding any solids.

instructions.title: Combine and Finish
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces, remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, and crushed fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi). Stir well. Simmer for 5 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the gravy's flavors. Finally, stir in the heavy cream until just heated through. Do not boil after adding cream.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and serve your classic Butter Chicken hot with naan bread, roti, or basmati rice. Enjoy this rich and flavorful Indian delicacy!

tips: For truly tender chicken, marinate it overnight in the refrigerator. The longer it marinates, the more flavor it will absorb.
Using good quality crushed tomatoes is crucial for the gravy's depth. Adding a pinch of sugar balances the acidity of the tomatoes beautifully.
Always add heavy cream at the very end and do not boil the curry after adding it, as this can cause the cream to curdle. Just heat it through gently.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in its native tongue as Murgh Makhani, is not just a dish; it's a global culinary phenomenon. This iconic Indian chicken recipe has charmed palates worldwide with its rich, creamy, and subtly sweet tomato-based gravy, making it a beloved staple in Indian restaurants and home kitchens alike. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken in your own home, you've come to the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through the history, ingredients, and step-by-step process to master this classic, ensuring an authentic and deeply satisfying experience.

## What is Classic Butter Chicken?

Classic Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter," a name that perfectly encapsulates its luxurious nature. Originating in Delhi, India, in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant, it was born from a clever improvisation. The chefs, looking for a way to use leftover tandoori chicken, simmered it in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was an instant classic, a dish that balanced the smoky notes of the chicken with a velvety, tangy, and mildly spiced sauce.

Its hallmark is the vibrant orange hue of the gravy, derived from tomatoes and a touch of Kashmiri red chili powder, which imparts color without excessive heat. The flavor profile is complex yet harmonious, featuring the tang of tomatoes, the sweetness of a touch of sugar, the warmth of garam masala, and the distinct aroma of fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi). This delightful interplay of flavors and textures makes Butter Chicken an unparalleled comfort food and a testament to the brilliance of Indian cuisine.

## Ingredients for Authentic Murgh Makhani

Crafting authentic Murgh Makhani begins with selecting quality ingredients. The beauty of Butter Chicken lies in the freshness and balance of its components.

For the Chicken Marinade:
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 teaspoon cumin powder
*   Salt to taste

For the Makhani Gravy:
*   2 tablespoons butter (plus more for cooking chicken)
*   1 tablespoon oil
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   4-5 medium tomatoes, pureed (or 1 can crushed tomatoes)
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional for extra creaminess)
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon sugar (or to taste, balances tang)
*   1 teaspoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream (or more, to taste)
*   Salt to taste
*   Water or chicken broth, as needed

For Garnish:
*   Fresh cream
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped

Using fresh, ripe tomatoes for the puree will yield a superior flavor, but good quality canned crushed tomatoes are an excellent alternative for convenience. The cashews are key to achieving that restaurant-style thick, smooth, and rich gravy.

## Step-by-Step: How to Make Butter Chicken

Making Butter Chicken from scratch is a rewarding process. Follow these steps for a truly memorable dish:

1.  **Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well, ensuring each piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, for maximum flavor absorption.

2.  **Cook the Chicken:** Heat a tablespoon of butter and a splash of oil in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Sear until lightly browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. The slight charring adds a wonderful smoky depth to the Butter Chicken. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

3.  **Prepare the Makhani Gravy Base:** In the same pan (add more butter/oil if needed), reduce heat to medium. Add the finely chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 5-7 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

4.  **Build the Gravy:** Stir in the pureed tomatoes (or crushed tomatoes) and the soaked cashews (if using). Add the red chili powder, garam masala, and turmeric powder. Mix well and cook, stirring occasionally, for 10-15 minutes, or until the tomatoes have cooked down, darkened in color, and the oil starts to separate from the mixture. This step is crucial for developing a deep, rich flavor.

5.  **Blend the Gravy:** Carefully transfer the cooked gravy mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth. For an extra velvety texture, you can strain the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan.

6.  **Finish the Gravy:** Return the smooth gravy to the pan over low-medium heat. Stir in the remaining butter, sugar, and salt to taste. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Crush the kasoori methi between your palms and add it to the gravy. This releases its aromatic oils, which are essential for the authentic taste of Butter Chicken.

7.  **Combine and Simmer:** Add the cooked chicken pieces to the simmering gravy. Stir gently to coat the chicken. Pour in the heavy cream and mix well. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the flavors of the gravy and heat through. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream, as it can curdle.

8.  **Garnish and Serve:** Ladle the hot Butter Chicken into serving bowls. Drizzle with a swirl of fresh cream and garnish generously with chopped fresh cilantro.

## Pro Tips for the Best Butter Chicken

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tricks:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The yogurt and spices tenderize the chicken and infuse it with flavor, making a significant difference to the final dish. Overnight marination is ideal.
*   **Charring the Chicken:** Whether you grill, pan-fry, or even bake your chicken, aim for some slightly charred edges. This replicates the tandoori effect and adds a fantastic smoky depth that is characteristic of authentic Butter Chicken.
*   **Smooth Gravy:** Blend your gravy thoroughly. If you desire an ultra-smooth texture, pass the blended gravy through a fine-mesh sieve to remove any remaining fibrous bits from the onions or tomatoes.
*   **Kasoori Methi is Non-Negotiable:** Dried fenugreek leaves (kasoori methi) are the secret ingredient that gives Butter Chicken its distinctive aroma and flavor. Don't omit it! Lightly toasting them in a dry pan for a few seconds before crushing them can enhance their fragrance.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust! The best Butter Chicken has a perfect balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Add a little more sugar if your tomatoes are very tart, or a squeeze of lemon juice if it needs more zing. Adjust salt and spice levels to your preference.
*   **Good Quality Butter and Cream:** Since these are prominent ingredients, using high-quality unsalted butter and fresh heavy cream will elevate the richness and texture of your Murgh Makhani considerably.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs beautifully with a variety of accompaniments, making it a complete and satisfying meal.

*   **Bread:** The classic choice is warm, fluffy naan bread, perfect for scooping up every last bit of that luscious gravy. Roti, paratha, or even plain pita bread also work wonderfully.
*   **Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps absorb the rich sauce.
*   **Salad and Raita:** A simple side salad of sliced cucumbers, onions, and tomatoes, perhaps with a squeeze of lemon, offers a refreshing counterpoint. A cooling raita (yogurt dip with cucumber and spices) can also balance the richness.
*   **Beverages:** A mango lassi (sweet yogurt drink) is a traditional and delightful pairing. For alcoholic beverages, a light lager or a crisp white wine can complement the flavors without overpowering them.

## Variations and Dietary Substitutions

The versatility of Murgh Makhani allows for several adaptations, catering to different dietary needs and preferences.

*   **Vegetarian Butter Chicken:** Easily transform this dish into Paneer Makhani by substituting the chicken with cubes of paneer (Indian cottage cheese). Tofu or mixed vegetables (like bell peppers, peas, and carrots) can also be used for a delicious vegetarian alternative.
*   **Vegan Butter Chicken:** For a plant-based version, replace butter with a plant-based butter alternative or oil, and use full-fat coconut cream or cashew cream instead of dairy cream. Plant-based yogurt can be used for the chicken marinade, or simply omit it for a vegan chicken substitute like seitan or jackfruit.
*   **Healthier Options:** To reduce the calorie count, use Greek yogurt in the marinade, opt for leaner chicken breast, and reduce the amount of cream, replacing some of it with milk or even a pureed vegetable like cauliflower for thickness.
*   **Spicier Butter Chicken:** If you prefer more heat, increase the amount of red chili powder in both the marinade and the gravy, or add a finely chopped green chili during the onion sautéing stage.

No matter how you choose to make it, homemade Butter Chicken is an experience that delights the senses. With this guide, you're well-equipped to create a dish that rivals any restaurant, bringing the authentic taste of Murgh Makhani right to your dining table. Enjoy the process, savor the aroma, and delight in every creamy, flavorful bite of this Indian culinary masterpiece.
